title: Climb into Mount Nimba's high grasslands with a guide
description: Dense lowland forest gives way to montane grassland on Guinea's highest massif, whose endemic wildlife includes a viviparous toad. The core area is a strict reserve and World Heritage site in danger, so arrange any visit through local authorities rather than treating it as an open trail.

title: Take a boat from Conakry to the Îles de Los
description: The forested islands sit just offshore from the capital and are one of the national tourism office's principal beach destinations. Boat conditions and return arrangements vary, so confirm both before leaving Conakry.

title: Walk to the cascade at Voile de la Mariée
description: A narrow sheet of water drops through greenery outside Kindia, giving the falls their bridal-veil name. Water volume changes markedly, so ask locally about recent conditions before making the detour.

title: Trek between escarpments and waterfalls in Fouta-Djalon
description: The highland plateau links deep valleys, grasslands and numerous river sources rather than a single signed route. Use a local trekking guide to connect villages and waterfalls and to check road and river conditions.

title: Look across the gorge at Kinkon Falls
description: The Kokoulo River plunges from the Fouta-Djalon plateau near Pita. The tourism guide identifies the falls but gives no operating details, so confirm the approach and safe viewpoint locally.

title: Cool off beside the cascades of Soumba
description: These rocky cascades provide a nature stop within reach of Conakry and are listed by the national tourism office among Dubréka's principal sites. Treat swimming as conditional on current flow and local advice.

title: Follow a local guide to Kambadaga Falls
description: Kambadaga is one of several named waterfall sites around Pita but receives far less attention than the region's headline falls. The official guide lists the site without access details, making local guidance essential.

title: Walk down to the cascades of Saala
description: Saala is a documented waterfall excursion from Labé in the Fouta-Djalon highlands. The tourism guide does not publish trail or water conditions, so go with someone who knows the current route.

title: Cross the channels of the Bijagós by boat
description: The World Heritage archipelago contains 88 islands and islets shaped by tides, estuaries and mangroves. Shallow banks make navigation part of the experience; use an experienced local operator and verify park permissions.

title: Track saltwater hippos with a guide on Orango
description: The Bijagós are the only place where hippos live in seawater on an almost permanent basis. Sightings are never guaranteed, and the park's community base at Anôr should be used to arrange a guided outing.

title: Watch green turtles nest on Poilão with park guides
description: Poilão holds Africa's most important green-turtle nesting beach, with tens of thousands of nests recorded in peak years. Access belongs inside a park-arranged trip; confirm the relevant nesting window and visitor rules before travel.

title: Trace the slave-trade history of Cacheu's fort and museum
description: Cacheu was an early Portuguese colonial capital and slave-trading port; the protected-area authority's visitor circuit links its fort, chapel and slavery museum. Begin at the park office to confirm access and find a guide.

title: Walk Cantanhez forest trails with a local guide
description: Cantanhez protects some of Guinea-Bissau's largest dense-forest blocks and habitat for chimpanzees, colobus monkeys and buffalo. Arrange a guide at IBAP or the park headquarters in Iemberém; wildlife sightings are not assured.

title: Paddle across Lagoa de Cufada to the birdwatching lookout
description: IBAP's documented route crosses Guinea-Bissau's largest freshwater lake by canoe to a lookout over the lake and forest. The park headquarters in Buba provides current information and local guides.

title: Paddle the Rio Blimbom through Cacheu's mangroves
description: This named park circuit threads mangroves, bird habitat and sacred forest near Cacheu. Boat visits depend on the tide, so arrange the canoe and timing at the Cacheu or São Domingos park office.

title: Canoe from Canamina into Cantanhez's forest mosaic
description: IBAP lists Canamina as a discovery trail combining dense forest, mangroves and primate habitat. It is a specific community-based route within Cantanhez, arranged through the park rather than an unsigned independent excursion.

title: Walk Chinguetti's lanes to its square-minaret mosque
description: Chinguetti grew as a caravan and Islamic-learning centre, with courtyard houses packed around a mosque whose square minaret rises from the old quarter. The mosque is an active religious site, so confirm respectful visitor boundaries locally.

title: Climb through the stone ruins of Ouadane's old ksar
description: Ouadane was one of four medieval caravan towns whose dense lanes and patio houses adapted urban life to the desert. Its old mosque is partly ruined, and local guidance helps distinguish conserved fabric from later settlement.

title: Cross the concentric ridges of the Richat Structure
description: The vast circular landform known as the Eye of Africa lies beyond Ouadane and makes sense on the ground as a sequence of rocky rings. Treat it as a remote guided desert journey and confirm vehicle, water and route conditions before departure.

title: Sail a traditional lanche through Banc d'Arguin
description: Shallow coastal waters, islands and mudflats support one of the world's great concentrations of migratory shorebirds. Motor craft are prohibited in the park's tourism guidance, so arrange a trip aboard an Imraguen sailing lanche and verify current permits.

title: Watch painted pirogues land at Nouakchott's fish market
description: Hundreds of brightly painted fishing boats return to the beach and unload directly into the market, making late afternoon the key moment. Keep clear of working crews and ask before photographing people at close range.

title: Ride alongside the desert iron-ore train
description: The railway carries iron ore from Zouérat to the mineral port at Nouadhibou across a long Saharan corridor. Passenger arrangements and safety conditions can change, so use an authorised local operator and verify the current way to travel before departure.

title: Rest beneath the palms at Terjit oasis
description: A spring-fed ribbon of palms occupies a narrow gorge in the Adrar and offers a striking pause between desert stages. The tourism office names Terjit as an oasis excursion from Atar but gives no fixed visitor arrangements, so confirm locally.

title: Camp beneath the granite monolith of Ben Amera
description: Ben Amera rises alone from the desert and is promoted by Mauritania's tourism office as a wilderness bivouac. Reaching it is a remote overland undertaking; arrange a knowledgeable driver and carry supplies appropriate to current conditions.
